title: slot-agility-slopebench-mini-report
body:
Summary:

This mini-report captures early slopebench runs focused on 'slot agility' — a lightweight experiment to measure how quickly the runtime can reassign GPU slots between sessions under changing concurrency, and the downstream effect on latency percentiles and per-token cost. Goal was to collect text-friendly charts and a concise set of recommendations for routing and prewarm heuristics.

Key takeaways:
- Fast slot reassignment (agility) reduces p99 latency amplification during modest concurrency ramps (2x to 6x) by ~18–30ms in these runs.
- There is a non-linear cost step when slot churn forces cold decoder state loads; optimize to avoid >12% extra per-token unit cost at short bursts.
- A small prewarm window (200–400ms) paired with opportunistic idle coalescing gives the best latency/cost tradeoff for our target interactive SLA.

Test setup:
- Benchmark name: slopebench-slot-agility-v1
- Model: open-llm-13B-fp16 (quantized emulation) with cached kv support enabled
- Hardware profile: a single A100-80GB equivalence (multi-tenant simulated slots), 4 logical slots used for multiplexing
- Client pattern: synthetic session arrivals (Poisson), per-session prompt length 40 tokens, response 120 tokens.
- Duration: 30m warm, 30m measurement window per scenario
- Metrics captured: p50/p90/p99 latency (ms) for generate() end-to-end, slot reassignment time (ms), extra per-token cost % vs steady baseline, CPU/GPU utilization sampled at 5s cadence

Workload scenarios (representative):
1) steady baseline: concurrency 2 sustained
2) modest ramp: 2 -> 6 sustained for 5m (2x to 6x)
3) spike-and-drop: sudden peak to concurrency 12 for 30s then back to 3
4) frequent small spikes: +1 concurrency every 20s for 10 cycles

Results (text tables):
Scenario | p50 (ms) | p90 (ms) | p99 (ms) | slot-reassign (ms) | delta cost (%)
Baseline   | 58      | 96      | 168     | 18                 | 0.0
Modest ramp| 64      | 112     | 186     | 26                 | +4.2
Spike short| 81      | 170     | 322     | 54                 | +11.8
Freq spikes| 70      | 138     | 254     | 42                 | +7.9

Observational chart (concurrency vs p99; simple ASCII slope):
Concurrency: 2  3  4   6   8   12
P99 (ms)   : 168 172 178 186 214 322
ASCII slope (approx):
  p99 
  350 |                          *
  300 |                     *    
  250 |                *         
  200 |            *             
  150 |      *                  
  100 |  *                     
       +----------------------
        2 3 4 6 8 12 (concurrency)

Cost sensitivity note (per 1M tokens baseline = $9.80):
- Baseline steady: $9.80 / 1M tokens
- Modest ramp (short-term): effective $10.22 (+4.2%) due to slot reshuffle overheads
- Spike short: effective $10.97 (+11.8%) when state loads happen repeatedly
- Frequent small spikes: $10.58 (+7.9%)

Detailed observations:
- Slot reassignment time correlates strongly with p90->p99 jump. When reassignment >40ms we see p99 amplify sharply. The underlying contributor is decoder state transfer combined with memory pressure evictions.
- Opportunistic coalescing of idle sessions (holding slots in a soft-reserve for 250–500ms) dramatically reduces reassign frequency on frequent small spikes and reduces cost by ~3–5% in that scenario.
- Aggressive prewarm (alloc + memory touch) reduces p99 for Spike short by ~28ms but increases baseline cost by ~1.4%.
- The 'sweet spot' for interactive workloads observed: prewarm window 200–400ms + soft-reserve TTL 300ms. This yielded p99 ~(baseline+18ms) while keeping cost delta <5% for modest ramps.

Recommendations (short):
- Implement a soft-reserve slot state that can be promoted without full decoder reload; TTL default 300ms, adjustable by customer SLA tier.
- Add a slope-aware routing heuristic: detect rising slope in arrival rate and preemptively allocate +1 slot per 3 sustained arrival/sec increase.
- Expose a user-config knob: prewarm aggressiveness (off / light / aggressive) with documented cost delta ranges. Default to 'light' for general hosted customers.

Open questions / next steps:
- Validate across model families (decoder-only 7B, 70B encoder-decoder) to calibrate prewarm cost multipliers.
- Re-run with real traffic trace from customer X (ENG-1294 linked) to confirm small-spike behavior maps to production.
- Prototype an in-memory 'quick-swap' path that avoids full KV rehydrate on promotion; estimate engineering effort 2w.

Appendix: raw numbers (sample of aggregated 5s buckets for modest ramp window):
- concurrency series (5s buckets): [2,2,3,3,4,5,6,6,6,6,5,4,4,3,3]
- p99 series (ms): [168,170,172,174,178,182,186,186,186,188,184,180,178,174,172]
- slot-reassign (ms) series: [20,22,26,24,28,30,26,26,24,28,22,20,18,22,24]

Notes-to-self / author log:
- Ran two variants of prewarm: memory-touch-only and full-kv-restore. Memory-touch is ~60% of benefit at ~25% of extra cost. Document that in follow-up.
- Share these quick slides with SEs next week; plan: one-pager for support playbook on slot soft-reserve.

raw_text_preview: Mini-run notes: slopebench v1. 30m windows. p99 climbs fastest when slot-reassign >40ms. Recommend soft-reserve TTL 300ms and slope-aware routing. Next: validate on real traces.
